perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s perspective, he knows/experienced:

- He is a construction worker at a construction company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist. They have a friendly, professional colleague relationship, often interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork/project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. Elizabeth told him no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and offered to listen or take a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During their coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as severe. Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He worried he might have embarrassed her or overstepped and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and reassured her of his support. Elizabeth said he didn’t overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available for chats or breaks. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
